asof: Settles Mon 9 Nov 2026 · written Tue 10 Nov
headline: Risk-on rebound sells the reds 5–5.5bp before CPI; the U7 peak at 4.445% now prices just over two hikes.
summary: The strip sold off again on Monday, led by the reds: M7 rose 5.5bp to 4.42%, H7 and U7 5bp to 4.32% and 4.445%, and Z7 4.5bp, while Z6 rose only 2bp to 4.165%, U6 held at 3.92% and the 2029 contracts H9–Z9 rose just 1bp to 4.335–4.35%. Two sessions have now retraced about 60–70% of last Thursday's rally in the reds, but from the 30 October settle M7 is still 6bp lower, U7 7.5bp and Z7 6.5bp, H7 3.5bp, the greens 5.5–6bp, and Z6 is 2bp higher. The peak stays in SR3U7 at 4.445%, 55.5bp over the 3.89% SOFR fixing, with 11bp of easing priced from there to Z9. Just over two hikes is a bit more than the consensus of a December move plus one more in early 2027.
drivers: Haven bid unwinds as stocks rebound

The S&P 500 rose 2.4% and the Nasdaq 2.7%, with chip stocks up more than 6% even as Nvidia fell about 6% on the probe into its CEO, after the S&P's worst week since April 2025. Selling of Treasuries as a hedge was led by short tenors, with the 2-year up as much as 5bp intraday to 4.57%. In SR3 that hit the reds hardest: H7–U7 rose 5–5.5bp in rate against 2bp in Z6.

The $58bn 3-year sale stopped at 4.627%, tailing the when-issued yield by 0.5bp, the biggest tail since May. Bid-to-cover fell to 2.53 from 2.62, the lowest since August 2025, and indirects took 55.5% against 57.6% last month, so dealers and directs had to absorb supply with $42bn of 10-years due Tuesday.
Fed hike bets rebuilt; Barkin keeps December open

FedWatch odds of a 9 December hike were about 79–81% on Monday, up from 71% a week earlier. Richmond's Barkin said the direction of policy is clear with inflation still the main risk, but that hikes should come with care and he has no base case for December. The reds took that as a nod to a gradual path: H7/M7 widened just 0.5bp to +10bp.
Oil slump keeps the greens anchored

Brent settled down nearly 6% at $92.57 after Trump called new strikes on Iran highly unlikely if talks progress, extending last week's 16% drop from above $112 at the start of the month. Lower energy prices capped inflation risk further out: Z8–Z9 rose just 1bp, so Z7/Z8 fell 3.5bp to −7bp. Tuesday's CPI is seen at 0.3% headline and 0.2% core month-on-month.
spreads: The reds sold off relative to both ends of the strip. U6/Z6 widened 2bp to +24.5bp and Z6/H7 3bp to +15.5bp (−5.5bp on the month), while H7/M7 rose 0.5bp to +10bp (−2.5bp) and M7/U7 slipped 0.5bp to +2.5bp (−1.5bp); U7/Z7 fell 0.5bp to −1.5bp, so U7 remains the peak by 1.5bp. Z6/Z7 widened 2.5bp to +26.5bp but is still 8.5bp tighter month-to-date, and Z6/M7 rose 3.5bp to +25.5bp (−8bp). Past the peak the inversion deepened: Z7/Z8 fell 3.5bp to −7bp and U7/Z8 4bp to −8.5bp (+0.5bp and +1.5bp on the month), with Z7/H8 at −2bp and the green consecutive spreads between −2bp and 0; Z8/Z9 held at −2.5bp. The H7/M7/U7 fly rose 1bp to +7.5bp and M7/U7/Z7 was unchanged at +4bp (−1bp and −2.5bp on the month). Week-to-date changes equal Monday's, as the week runs from Friday's settle.
fed: The latest weekday fed funds futures snapshot is Friday's, after payrolls: 19bp for the 9 December meeting (a 76% chance of a hike), 24bp by January, 34bp by March, 43.9bp by June and a 47bp peak by September 2027 (implied EFFR 4.35%). That is up from 16.2bp, 20.5bp, 30.5bp, 40.4bp and a 43.5bp peak on Thursday, but against the 30 October month-end, which is also a week earlier (17.6bp, 24bp, 37.3bp, 52.1bp, 57bp peak), only December is higher and the 2027 path is still 3–10bp lower. Monday's SR3 settles go further than that snapshot: the 4.35% ZQ peak plus SOFR's 1bp premium over the 3.88% EFFR is 4.36%, 8.5bp under U7 at 4.445%, and Z6 at 4.165% is 3.5bp over January ZQ plus that premium, which fits the 79–81% December odds FedWatch showed on Monday. With most bank economists calling for a December hike and September's projections showing one more move this year, SR3's just-over-two-hike peak is a touch rich; Tuesday's CPI decides whether December is fully priced.

ideas.title: Stay short the H7/M7 calendar spread (fade 2027 hikes)
ideas.why: Open at +10bp, 1bp against entry: H7 rose 5bp and M7 5.5bp in rate on Monday, a second parallel selloff after Friday's, so the rebound lifted the whole 2027 path rather than front-loading it. Barkin's call for a careful pace and the market moving the last hike to April keep the case for a narrower March–June gap; 7bp to target against 3bp to the stop.
ideas.risk: A hot core CPI on Tuesday could add hikes beyond April and push the spread through +13bp.

ideas.title: Keep 2028 easing as the hedge: sell Z7, buy Z8 (stop tightened)
ideas.why: Open at −7bp, now just 1bp from entry after falling 3.5bp on Monday as Z7 rose 4.5bp in rate and Z8 only 1bp: the risk-on selloff hit the reds and left the greens anchored by cheaper oil, which is what the hedge is for. We lower the stop to −3bp from +1bp to lock in that move and extend the target to −13bp, so reward is 1.5 times risk from here.
ideas.risk: A soft CPI that revives the haven bid in the reds would push the spread back above −3bp.

ideas.title: Stay neutral the front contract through refunding settlement

levels.Why neutral: fixings, not the Fed, drive it now

ideas.why: U6 held at 96.080 (3.92% implied) for a third session, against the 3.89% SOFR fixing for 6 November, 1bp under the 3.90% interest on reserves, 1bp over the 3.88% EFFR and 11bp under the 4.00% standing repo rate. Refunding notes, including Monday's 3-year sale, settle on 16 November and only U6's last week sees the December decision, so there is little to gain from an outright view.
ideas.risk: If refunding settlement tightens funding, SOFR could print back near 3.95% and cost a couple of bp.

watch: Consensus 0.3% headline and 0.2% core month-on-month after 0.6% and 0.3% in September, with no annual rate published; it sets Z6, the December odds and the H7/M7 core. $42bn of 10-years follows.
Cash bond market closed and no SOFR fixing; SR3 liquidity thin.
$25bn after Monday's weak 3-year sale; term premium and the greens.

Another AI-stock slide would revive the haven bid in the reds; a breakdown in Iran talks that lifts Brent back toward $100 would add to 2027 inflation risk.
